claim_or_location: chr17p_loss hallmark frequency per study/sample (notes: 'chr17p loss 0.28 / 0.04 / 0.30 / 0.74 / 0.30 / 0.04')
evidence: 06_cnv_aggregate.py computes `mal[e].astype(bool).mean()`; chr17p_loss is NaN for 63,694 cells (8 samples where no window maps to 17p: okada__586_pons 23,611 cells, okada__1734_pons 8,486, okada__1656_pons 4,026, labelle__H3K27M_P9 6,366, jessa_scrna__P-3407 5,801, jessa_scrna__P-4198 4,361, collot__PMC-DMG-7 5,623, collot__PMC-DMG-8 4,979) and NaN.astype(bool) is True. Recomputed fraction of CNV-malignant cells with chr17p_loss==True: okada 0.030 (table 0.300), collot 0.000 (table 0.742), jessa_scrna 0.177 (table 0.276), labelle 0.707 (table 0.803); unaffected studies match (desisto 0.614, filbin 0.043, jessa_multiome 0.038, liu 0.303). Per-sample table frac_malignant_chr17p_loss = 1.0 for all 8 affected samples.
impact_on_conclusions: The chr17p_loss column of cnv_event_frequencies.csv and malignant_calls_per_sample.csv, and the corresponding sentence in the notes, are wrong for okada, collot, jessa_scrna and labelle; the headline 'Collot 17p loss 0.74' is an artefact.
recommendation: Use `mal[e].eq(True).mean()` (or fillna(False)) and report the number of cells for which the event could be evaluated; regenerate both tables and the notes paragraph.

claim_or_location: Arm-level hallmark events computed from 100-gene chromosome-wide windows assigned to an arm by their mean position
evidence: Windows are built per chromosome (infercnvpy _running_mean_by_chromosome), not per arm, so windows straddle the centromere. Reconstructed for jessa_scrna__P-6337 (7,021 genes): chr17 has 396 used genes of which 82 on 17p; only 5 of 30 windows are labelled 17p and they contain 82%, 72%, 62%, 52%, 42% p-arm genes; chr10: 2 of 14 windows labelled 10p (72%, 62% p genes). 18p is absent in all 117 samples; 9p absent in 14 samples; in low-gene samples most p arms vanish (okada__1734_pons: 17 arms missing, 22 windows total; labelle__H3K27M_P9: 13 arms missing, 41 windows; okada__586_pons 10 arms missing). For jessa_scrna__P-3407 (3,667 genes own cells) the first chr17 window spans 0.6-61 Mb.
impact_on_conclusions: 17p-loss (TP53 locus) and other short-arm events are diluted by q-arm genes and unavailable in 8 samples (63,694 cells); arm means (arm_17p, arm_10q, ...) in malignant_calls.csv are not clean arm estimates. Large-arm events (1q, 13q, 14q, chr2, chr7) are little affected.
recommendation: Smooth per arm (pass arm as the 'chromosome' key to the running mean, or use infercnvpy with arm-level var), or compute arm means from gene-level values; record per sample which arms were evaluable.

claim_or_location: '4q12 gain' (PDGFRA/KIT) hallmark; notes: 'Filbin ... 1.00 (Filbin: 1 of 9 patients dominates)'
evidence: 4q12 is represented by 0-2 windows per sample (median 1; zero in 5 samples). In filbin__BCH1126 the single 4q12 window spans chr4:37.6-81.7 Mb (100 genes, 19 inside 52.7-59.5 Mb). PDGFRA mean log-expression is 0.00 in reference vs 1.29 in non-reference cells (LNX1 0.00 vs 0.53, CHIC2 0.11 vs 0.67, SCFD2 0.22 vs 0.87): the window measures OPC-lineage expression against an immune reference. z is computed with the reference SD floored at 0.01, so one window suffices for z>=2. Recomputed per-sample frequency in Filbin: all 9 samples 0.97-1.00 (not 'one patient dominates'); Spearman rho(arm_4q12, score_OPC_like) among malignant cells: liu 0.38, desisto 0.34, filbin 0.20, okada 0.16. Published PDGFRA amplification/activation prevalence in DMG is ~20-30%.
impact_on_conclusions: chr4q12_gain frequencies (Filbin 1.00, LaBelle 0.59, Liu 0.34, Desisto 0.44) are not credible as focal amplification calls and the Filbin sentence in the notes is false; 4q12 also contributes to malignant calls as a hallmark event.
recommendation: Drop 4q12 from the hallmark set or call it from gene-level (unsmoothed) deviations restricted to the band with a lineage-matched reference; correct the notes.

claim_or_location: Tier-3 'author-independent' agreement (0.946-0.987) presented as 'the meaningful one'; Liu crosstab 'all TME classes -> 0 malignant; malignant states -> 0 normal'
evidence: tier3_cnv_marker_agree is evaluated only on cells where marker_call and cnv_call agree: 43,266/84,194 (51%) jessa_scrna, 81,584/161,043 (51%) okada, 4,844/8,705 liu. The excluded cells are the hard ones: among cnv_call=malignant & marker_call=normal cells with an author label (42,941), 34,046 (79%) are author-malignant (jessa_scrna: oligodendrocyte-type 5,503/5,594, neuron-type 3,152/3,249 author-malignant). The Liu consensus crosstab is tautological: consensus_call requires author agreement, so 0 of 228,643 labelled non-ambiguous cells disagree with the author by construction; the cnv_call crosstab shows e.g. OC-like 380 malignant/129 normal, Myeloid 114 malignant/576 normal.
impact_on_conclusions: Readers are given an agreement figure on a self-selected easy half of the cells and a crosstab that cannot show disagreement; the notes over-state validation strength.
recommendation: Report tier-3 coverage as a fraction and the author composition of the excluded cells; replace the Liu consensus crosstab with the cnv_call crosstab (tier 2) or label it as 'by construction'.

claim_or_location: 'ambiguous' tier-3 class (100,880 cells, 29.5%) and its downstream mapping to lineage_label 'Unknown'
evidence: Decomposition of ambiguous cells: marker/CNV disagreement 62,153; marker+author disagreement 20,851; author-only disagreement 17,435; unassigned 441. The dominant pattern is cnv_call=malignant with marker_call=normal (okada 21,980; jessa_scrna 10,526; jessa_multiome 6,985), 79% of which are author-malignant. Jessa author cell types most often ambiguous: Oligodendrocytes 49.3% (6,952/14,106), Neurons 44.9%, Vascular 34.3%, Astrocytes 27.8%, OPC 20.7%. Liu OC-like 293/509 ambiguous. 07_assemble_atlas_input.py maps ambiguous -> 'Unknown' and only consensus_call=='malignant' enters the malignant compartment.
impact_on_conclusions: The malignant compartment used in Phases 4-6 (scANVI labels, malignant scVI, metaprograms, cell2location reference) is depleted of OC-like and neuron-like tumour cells in a state-dependent way; downstream state frequencies (OC-like, neuron-like) are biased low.
recommendation: Either trust cnv_call for marker-normal glial/neuronal cells when the cluster carries a hallmark event, or report the state bias explicitly and test metaprogram results with tier-2 labels as sensitivity.

file: docs/phase3_cnv_notes.md (design table, 'Deviations / caveats'); src/dmg_atlas/cnv.py comments; logs/phase3_cnv.log; results/qc/cnv_cluster_stats_vs_author.csv
claim_or_location: 'Thresholds ... tuned against Jessa author labels (seven scRNA samples)'; 'Okada and Collot labels were not used for tuning'; '7-sample Jessa scRNA benchmark recall 0.986 / precision 0.973'; 'all in logs/phase3_cnv.log'
evidence: The log's benchmark-subset runs (17:03-17:16) process 9 jessa_scrna samples (P-1713, P-3407, P-4198, P-4504, P-6254, P-6328, P-6337, P-6519, P-6640; 60,047 cells), 7 okada samples (66,595 cells), 4 jessa_multiome and 2 collot samples. results/qc/cnv_cluster_stats_vs_author.csv, cited in cnv.py as the basis of score_floor, contains author-labelled clusters from okada (264), jessa_multiome (104), liu (98) and collot (60). The log contains no recall/precision values (grep 'recall|precision|agreement' -> none), so the design-table numbers are unverifiable. No 7-of-9 combination of the final calls reproduces recall 0.986 (best 0.940); final recall on the 9 benchmark samples is 0.913, precision 0.975. Marker-threshold tuning sample is given as P-6337 in the notes and P-6251 in cnv.py.
impact_on_conclusions: The independence claimed for Okada/Collot validation is not supported, and the benchmark performance quoted in the design table is not the performance of the delivered pipeline.
recommendation: State the actual tuning set (9 Jessa scRNA + 7 Okada + 4 multiome + 2 Collot samples), remove or re-derive the 0.986/0.973 numbers from the final outputs, reconcile the tuning-sample statement.

claim_or_location: Circularity check: tier-2 agreement on tuning vs held-out samples
evidence: Pooled cell-level tier-2 agreement, benchmark vs held-out samples: jessa_scrna 0.912 (9 samples) vs 0.916 (8); jessa_multiome 0.888 (4) vs 0.946 (6); okada 0.860 (7) vs 0.850 (15); collot 0.852 (2) vs 0.946 (3). Median per-sample agreement jessa_scrna 0.941 (bench) vs 0.888 (held-out).
impact_on_conclusions: No evidence that threshold tuning inflated the pooled Jessa agreement; the benchmark set contained the hardest samples, so held-out agreement is similar or higher. The caveat in the notes is adequate once the tuning set is correctly described.
recommendation: Add this split to the validation table.

claim_or_location: Agreement reported as pooled cell-level fractions per study without CIs or a sample-level summary
evidence: Across 97 labelled samples the per-sample tier-2 agreement has median 0.899 (IQR 0.835-0.963, min 0.034); the cell-weighted mean is 0.882 but the unweighted sample-level mean is 0.837 (bootstrap 95% CI 0.793-0.876). Okada (161,043 cells, 47% of labelled cells) dominates the pooled figures.
impact_on_conclusions: Cells are pseudo-replicates; the unit of replication is the sample/patient. Pooled figures overstate typical per-sample performance by ~4-5 points.
recommendation: Report sample-level median/IQR and CI alongside pooled values; weight studies equally in the summary.

claim_or_location: Malignant clusters called on cnv_score elevation alone (no hallmark event)
evidence: 49,499 of 237,752 author-labelled CNV-malignant cells (20.8%) sit in clusters with no hallmark event; their author-malignant fraction is 0.847 vs 0.954 for event-backed clusters (collot 0.466 n=388; jessa_multiome 0.483 n=1,137; okada 0.829 n=36,963). okada__1734_pons (1,160 genes, 22 windows): 6,097 of 6,732 malignant-cluster cells are score-only. Sensitivity: raising the floor to 0.016 flips 32,284 cells (12.4% of CNV-malignant) to normal; lowering it to 0.004 flips 8,716 normal cells to malignant.
impact_on_conclusions: About one fifth of CNV-malignant calls rest on a single absolute threshold whose precision is materially lower; results in low-complexity nuclei samples are threshold-driven.
recommendation: Add a per-cell confidence flag (event-backed vs score-only); mark samples with < ~3,000 genes / < 100 windows as low-confidence; report sensitivity to the floor.

claim_or_location: z-scores for hallmark events
evidence: The noise filter sets |x| < 1.5 SD to 0 before reference statistics are computed, so reference arm means are ~0 and the per-cell SD collapses to the 0.01 floor; cluster z values of 14-22 for 1q gain (filbin__BCH1126 clusters) show that z>=2 is in practice an absolute deviation of >=0.02 log units. z is computed against per-cell SD, not the SE of a cluster mean, which is conservative, but the floor makes the 'z' label misleading.
impact_on_conclusions: Does not change calls but the thresholds should be described as absolute deviations.
recommendation: Describe thresholds in deviation units or compute z before noise filtering.

claim_or_location: Best-match baseline and reference refinement
evidence: Each cell keeps the reference category with the smallest mean |deviation| (min over 2-5 noisy baselines), which shrinks CNV signal for every cell, including reference cells whose own category mean includes them (min_ref_per_type=10 -> up to 10% self-weight). MAD refinement removes high-score reference cells after the category means were computed, so removed cells still shape the baseline.
impact_on_conclusions: Small downward bias of cnv_score for all cells and slightly optimistic reference statistics; direction is conservative for calling.
recommendation: Compute category means leave-one-out for reference cells or exclude a cell's own category; recompute means after MAD refinement.

claim_or_location: Centromere coordinates typed from memory
evidence: chr1 (121.7-125.1 Mb), chr2 (91.8-96.0 Mb) and chr17 (22.7-27.4 Mb) match the UCSC hg38 cytoBand acen rows quoted in UCSC mailing-list/GitHub copies of the table; all 24 entries agree with the auditor's independent recollection of the acen intervals; every midpoint lies in a protein-coding-gene-free gap of >=2.8 Mb (table re-read; chr22 0.16 Mb, acrocentric). Landmark genes fall on the expected side (EGFR 7p, PDGFRA/KIT 4q, ROCK1 18q first gene after the chr18 gap at 20.95 Mb).
impact_on_conclusions: Arm assignment of genes is correct; the typed coordinates are not a source of error. The real arm problem is the windowing (CNV-02).
recommendation: Replace with the UCSC file when network allows; otherwise acceptable.

claim_or_location: In-process inferCNV arithmetic
evidence: run_infercnv imports infercnvpy's _running_mean_by_chromosome (chromosomes natural-sorted chr1..chr22, genes sorted by start, pyramidal window 100 step 10, 'valid' convolution, single uniform window if genes < window); deviation clipped to +-3 before smoothing, per-cell median centring, noise filter 1.5 x global SD, matching infercnvpy's lfc_cap/dynamic_threshold. _window_positions reproduces the window->gene index mapping (lo=k*step, hi=lo+100; single window when G<100). No off-by-one found.
impact_on_conclusions: The smoothing arithmetic is infercnvpy's as stated; the notes' phrase 'own implementation' is slightly overstated (the core function is imported).
recommendation: None.

No titles inside panels (house rule met). Reference rows in P-6337 show MHC-region (chr6p) blocks and a focal chr4 signal in some reference cells.

evidence: Legend reports n=104,770 / 26,042 (all labelled Jessa cells) but 60,000 cells are plotted (random subsample, stated nowhere); author-Normal points are drawn after Malignant and hide them at low cnv_score; axis labels and units are present; no in-panel title.

claim_or_location: Pooled reference leakage
evidence: Pooled immune/lineage references come from other samples of the same study and assay stratum, excluding the sample's own barcodes; two patients have two samples in one study (collot PMC-DMG-9 core/edge; liu SUDIPG50Aut/Bio), so a sample can receive reference cells from the same patient. Author labels are not used in reference selection. Lineage candidates are purged only by CNV evidence against an immune anchor (stage A, z>=5), so weak-CNV tumour cells can enter pooled lineage references (notes acknowledge for own-sample candidates).
impact_on_conclusions: No label leakage; same-patient reference cells are normal cells and benign. Residual tumour contamination of pooled lineage references would reduce sensitivity, not inflate it.
recommendation: Exclude same-patient samples from pools for cleanliness.

claim_or_location: Fallback state gene sets (Phase 6 use only)

impact_on_conclusions: No effect on Phase 3; provenance is weak for any Phase 6 use of the fallback.
recommendation: Cite the exact supplementary tables and load them from files.

claim_or_location: Hallmark frequency sentence
evidence: All hallmark fractions other than chr17p (CNV-01) and the Filbin 4q12 remark (CNV-03) match cnv_event_frequencies.csv to two decimals (chr1q 0.46/0.54/0.20/0.59/0.43/0.49/0.88/0.93; chr2 0.06/0.20/0.04/0.22/0.55/0.26; chr7 0.13/0.37/0.22/0.06/0.36/0.71; 13q 0.27/0.29/0.13/0.14/0.21/0.24; 14q 0.19/0.52/0.16/0.75/0.34/0.34; 10q 0.20/0.24/0.13/0.02/0.16/0.28). Frequencies are 'fraction of CNV-malignant cells' pooled across samples, not per patient, so a single large sample dominates (okada 586_pons = 19% of all okada malignant cells); the per-sample '__frac_samples' columns exist but are not reported.
impact_on_conclusions: Cell-level pooling is not comparable with the patient-level frequencies of published genomics (e.g. PDGFRA 20-30% of patients).
recommendation: Report the fraction of samples (>=20% of malignant cells) alongside cell fractions.

claim_or_location: LaBelle values stored as layers['tpm'] and described as TPM; note claims 'P9 is a 10x library distributed as per-cell CPM (nCount_RNA = 1e6)'
evidence: All three GSE227983 tables are log2(TPM/10+1), not linear TPM: first 6 columns of tumor_ss2 have column sums 8,257-12,624, max 8.0-8.65, 100% fractional non-zeros; immune_ss2 sums 4,183-5,391; immune_tenx (P9 source) sums 3,661-6,177, max 7.6-9.0. Inverting (2^x-1)*10 gives 2.0e5-3.0e5 per cell (TPM over a gene-filtered table). qc_per_sample.csv median_counts for LaBelle SS2 samples = 4,823-9,527 and for P9 = 3,244, versus exactly 1e6 for every Filbin sample.
impact_on_conclusions: The Phase 2 deliverable mislabels a log-scale matrix as TPM and the note is factually wrong (nCount is ~3e3, not 1e6). Downstream phases detected the scale heuristically (cnv.py / 10_prepare_queries.py: rowmax<30 => log2), so atlas conclusions are not affected, but any consumer of labelle.qc.h5ad['tpm'] without that heuristic would be off by orders of magnitude.
recommendation: Rename the layer (e.g. 'log2_tpm10') or invert to linear TPM at ingest; record the scale in uns and var; correct the note (P9 CPM/1e6 claim) and the qc_report 'median counts' column for TPM cohorts.

claim_or_location: README: 'every results/ file is produced by a script in scripts/'; Phase 1 notes describe label tables built from supplementary xlsx and downloads from Zenodo (Collot scRNA), ScPCA portal (API token) and UCSC Cell Browser (Okada)
evidence: grep over scripts/ and notebooks/: no script writes data/interim/labels/ (02_build_sample_manifest.py only reads them); no script references zenodo.org, scpca-portal or cells-test.gi.ucsc.edu; 01_fetch_tumour_geo.py queues cover only GEO. MANIFEST_tumour.csv nevertheless contains 3 collot, 4 scpca and 13 okada rows and per_sample_summary.csv (okada) feeds the manifest. These steps exist only in the sub-agent's kernel.
impact_on_conclusions: Sample inclusion (H3 status, assay, site) for Jessa, Collot, DeSisto, LaBelle rests on label tables with no generating code; a third party cannot regenerate the manifest from the raw deposits.
recommendation: Add scripts (or a documented notebook) that parse the supplementary xlsx/docx into data/interim/labels/*.csv and that fetch Collot/ScPCA/Okada, recording checksums; keep the label_source column.

claim_or_location: Per-cell thresholds flag 8,486 of 15,228 nuclei of okada__1734_pons as qc_pass; the sample enters the atlas with 8,466 nuclei (2.7% of the 311,618-cell reference)
evidence: obs of okada.qc.h5ad: 1734_pons n_genes median 321 (IQR 249-452), n_counts median 351, 6,665 (43.8%) fail low_genes; passing nuclei have median 427 genes / 468 UMI, versus 971-2,805 genes in the other 21 Okada samples (next lowest 586_pons 971). No sample-level quality flag exists in qc_per_sample.csv or qc_report.md; the author QC (nFeature>200) is equally permissive.

claim_or_location: Notes: Liu has 'two annotations in the deposit' (32,617 / 23,686 genes) and only 'Filbin / LaBelle TPM tables contain no MT- genes'; Liu frozen nuclei are QC'd with the smartseq2 class (mito < 20%)
evidence: gene_harmonisation.csv: Liu raw files come in three annotations: 23,686 genes (16 samples, 4,007 unmapped), 32,617 (20 samples, 1,749 unmapped) and 55,765 (6 samples, 22,216 unmapped). All 16 samples on the 23,686-gene annotation (5,375 cells, all author_prep = frozen_nuclei) have pct_mito identically 0 for every cell (max 0.0), i.e. the annotation lacks MT- genes and the mito filter is inoperative (visible as flat markers in qc_violin_liu.png). Among frozen nuclei that do carry MT genes, 138 of 680 passing nuclei (20.3%) have 5-20% mito and would fail the project's own nuclei rule.
impact_on_conclusions: QC is heterogeneous within the Liu cohort (mito-filtered vs unfiltered samples; nuclei judged by the cell threshold). Liu is projection-only, so reference models are unaffected, but Liu-based comparisons (fresh vs frozen, pediatric vs adult) carry a QC confound that the notes do not disclose.
recommendation: State the three annotations and MT-gene absence in the notes; add a per-sample 'mt_genes_present' column to qc_per_sample.csv; apply the nuclei mito rule (or author_prep-aware rule) to frozen nuclei where MT genes exist.

claim_or_location: Manifest is the output of 02_build_sample_manifest.py
evidence: Re-ran the script to a temporary path and diffed: 239 cells differ. k27m_status differs for the 10 Jessa H3.3-G34R/V samples (disk 'WT', script output 'unknown' because jessa_excl() sets WT only when h3_variant == 'WT'); 229 further cells are float-vs-int formatting (age_years, n_cells_deposited) indicating the file was re-saved via pandas after generation. File mtime 13:44 vs script mtime 13:33; no doc records the edit.
impact_on_conclusions: No effect on the atlas (G34 samples are excluded out-group) and 'WT' is a defensible K27 status for G34 tumours, but the on-disk manifest is not reproducible from the code.
recommendation: Encode the G34 -> k27m_status='WT' rule in jessa_excl()/common and regenerate the manifest from the script.

claim_or_location: 'per-study medians 0.19 ScPCA to 0.63 Zang'; 'called 0 doublets in most samples'; predicted_doublet_fixed (score > 0.25) 'gives 0.1-2.6% per study'
evidence: qc_per_sample.csv (95 UMI samples with a threshold): per-study median auto-thresholds are ScPCA 0.19, DeSisto 0.28, multiome 0.38, Zang 0.38, scRNA 0.39, Okada 0.42, Collot 0.51 (no study at 0.63); 36/96 samples (37.5%) have 0 auto-called doublets (median per-sample rate 0.0003). Fixed-threshold pooled rates: DeSisto 0.08%, Zang 0.50%, Collot 1.06%, Okada 2.55% (claim verified). claim_or_location: Headline '2 replicated metaprograms' triggers the build-plan checkpoint ('fewer than 3 replicate across assays -> assay-dependence headline'). Sensitivity reported as 1/1/2/5 at cuts 0.75/0.80/0.85/0.90.

impact_on_conclusions: Nearly a third of the cNMF/composition input is classifier-rescued ambiguous cells, and the rescue rate is itself assay-dependent, so part of the nuclei-only programme structure (e.g. MP16 immune, MP15 cilia, nuclei-only OPC/AC-like MPs scoring higher in myeloid cells, MC-08) may come from the selection rather than from tumour biology.
recommendation: Report the selection breakdown per assay in §1; re-run the metaprogram clustering on consensus-malignant cells only as a sensitivity analysis; report how many member programmes of each MP come from samples with a high scanvi_only share.

claim_or_location: 'AC-like and OC-like/COP programmes are shared across assays once assay-biased genes are masked' (17 MPs, 4 replicated).
evidence: Masked set = 6,080 of 13,185 tested genes (46 %). Remaining genes per programme after masking: nuclei median 21 (min 0; 33 programmes < 10 genes, 12 < 5), cells median 34.5; the same absolute cut 0.85 is applied. Circularity: the mask is by construction the set of genes that differ between the assays (Welch 4 vs 23 samples, where 2 of the 4 cell samples are the two paired patients), so a cross-assay re-test after removing them is partly tautological. mMP2 ('OC-like/COP') is replicated with only 2 cell samples. Control run by the auditor: masking the same number of randomly chosen genes per programme (10 seeds) gives 2-3 MPs and 1 replicated, so the gain is specific to the masked gene identities and NOT a set-size artefact.
impact_on_conclusions: The masked result is reproducible and not a size artefact, but it cannot distinguish 'technical assay bias removed' from 'biological differences removed'; the claim that AC-like/OC-like are shared should be stated as conditional on removing nearly half the transcriptome, and the OC-like replication rests on 2 cell samples. Note also that unmasked clustering already merges OC-like/AC-like across assays at cut 0.86-0.87 (MC-02).
recommendation: Present the masked analysis as exploratory; add the random-mask control to the table; require >= 2 samples per assay class for 'replicated' and report it; consider restricting the mask to genes with a known nuclear-retention / intronic mechanism rather than all DE genes.

recommendation: Report the ratios for every MP; use a per-gene filter (e.g. remove genes whose UCell rank in myeloid exceeds that in malignant cells) or lower the fold threshold and show sensitivity.

claim_or_location: k* = largest k in 4..9 with silhouette >= 0.90 and every consensus cluster present in >= 80 % of restarts.
evidence: k_selection.csv: silhouette >= 0.90 holds for 71.3 % of all (sample, k) pairs (median silhouette 1.000 at k = 4, 5, 6; 0.913 at k = 9), so the silhouette criterion is rarely binding and the rule reduces to 'largest k that passes restart coverage'. Chosen k: 5 (1 sample), 6 (5), 7 (15), 8 (11), 9 (22 = 41 % at the ceiling). Auditor re-ran consensus NMF for k = 4..12 on desisto__1196 and okada__1963_pons: k = 10, 11, 12 fail the coverage criterion (min restart frac 0.2-0.7), so k* stays 9 in both - the ceiling is not binding in these two (provisional, 2 of 22 ceiling samples). Many sklearn NMF fits reach max_iter = 500 without meeting tol = 1e-4 (ConvergenceWarning).
impact_on_conclusions: Programme granularity is driven by the search range and restart coverage rather than by a stability optimum; it affects how many programmes enter the clustering but the 2-sample test suggests the ceiling is not systematically binding.
recommendation: Document that the silhouette criterion is non-discriminative; extend the range to 12 for a subset or report coverage curves; raise max_iter or record non-convergence.

These are malignant_selected cells with consensus_call 'ambiguous' (4,269) or 'normal' (12) that the malignant scVI model never embedded. Line `Z = normalize(np.nan_to_num(...))` zeroes them, so 4,281 cells collapse onto one point and their cosine neighbours are tie-broken arbitrarily. Recomputed on the 10,719 cells with a finite latent (same code path for all four embeddings): scVI acc 0.819 (table 0.629), nuclei→cells 0.822 (0.622), same-assay 0.931 (0.678; expected 0.765), same-sample 0.413 (0.295). claim_or_location: Within-section variance of Fisher z uses n_spots as independent observations.
evidence: Spots are spatially autocorrelated, so 1/(n−3) understates within-section variance by a large factor; however I² ≈ 0.99 and tau² (0.06-0.15) dominates the pooled variance, so the RE CIs and p_re are effectively between-section statistics and change little. BH is applied to the 30 DMG state×TME pairs only; the 11 within-section brainstem RE tests and the GBM pairs are uncorrected (p_re there are ≤1e-5 for the reported effects, so this is immaterial).
impact_on_conclusions: No material effect.
recommendation: Mention in methods.
